questions.q: Answer in one word: (I) What is the method of voting used in the election of the President of India? (II) For how long can the Vice-President act as President in the absence of a sitting President?
questions.answer: (I) Proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote (secret ballot) (II) Six months

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Explain the number of judges, including the Chief Justice, in the Supreme Court of India.
questions.answer: (1) As provided in the Constitution, the Supreme Court of India consists of the Chief Justice and other Judges whose number is prescribed by the Parliament from time to time. The Chief Justice and other Judges are appointed by the President. (2) In 1950 there was a Chief Justice and 7 judges; the number has been increased with need — the textbook gives a Chief Justice and 30 judges.

questions.q: Explain the importance of a no-confidence motion in the Indian Parliament in two points.
questions.answer: (1) If the Lok Sabha passes a ‘no-confidence motion’, the entire Council of Ministers including PM has to resign. (2) It means that if they lose the confidence of the Lok Sabha, the Council of Ministers is dislodged with the resignation of the Prime Minister.

questions.q: Mention any two qualifications required to be elected as President of India.
questions.answer: (1) To be eligible to be a member of the Rajya Sabha, a person must (a) be a citizen of India, and (b) be at least 30 years of age. (ii) (a) be a citizen of India (b) have completed the age of 35 years (c) be qualified for being elected as a Member of Lok Sabha (d) not hold any office of profit (2) (iii) be qualified for being elected as a member of the House of the People (Lok Sabha); and (iv) not hold any office of profit under the government of India, any State government or under any local authority or any other authority of the said government.

questions.q: Describe any two powers of the Prime Minister related to the Council of Ministers.
questions.answer: (1) No money bill can be introduced in the Lok Sabha without his/her prior recommendation. But in practice, it is the Prime Minister who makes and unmakes the Council of Ministers. It is on his/ her recommendations that the President appoints the members of the Council of Ministers and distributes portfolios among them. (2) He/She presides over the meetings of the Cabinet and communicates its decisions to the President. If, due to any reason, he/she submits his/her resignation, the entire Council of Ministers stands dissolved.

questions.q: How do both Houses of Parliament maintain control over the Council of Ministers? Highlight two ways.
questions.answer: (1) (a) By asking questions and supplementary questions: The first hour of every working day of Parliament relates to Question Hour in which the Ministers have to answer the questions raised by the members. (d) (i) ask questions and supplementary questions, (ii) adjournment motion and calling attention (2) (b) By discussing and passing motions: Calling Attention Motion, Adjournment Motion or Censure Motion can be moved and policies of the government can be debated and criticized. But only the Lok Sabha has the power to pass a no-confidence motion which if done, the Council of Minister resigns.

questions.q: Differentiate between direct and indirect elections in India with examples.
questions.answer: The members of the Lok Sabha are directly elected by the people of India. He/She is indirectly elected by an Electoral College consisting of the elected members of both the Houses of the Parliament and the State Legislative Assemblies.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Explain any three executive powers of the President of India.
questions.answer: (1) All executive actions of the government of India are carried out in his/her name. He/She also appoints other members of the Council of Ministers on the recommendations of the Prime Minister. (2) Appoints Governors, the Attorney General, the CAG, ambassadors, the UPSC, the Chief Justice and judges of the Supreme Court and High Courts and Election Commissioners, and can remove many of them as provided. (3) Moreover, the President is the supreme commander of the Armed Forces and appoints the Chiefs of the three wings, Army, Airforce and Navy. All diplomatic work is conducted and all international treaties and agreements are negotiated and concluded in his/her name.

questions.q: Explain the functions of the Prime Minister.
questions.answer: (1) It is on his/ her recommendations that the President appoints the members of the Council of Ministers and distributes portfolios among them. He/She presides over the meetings of the Cabinet and communicates its decisions to the President. (2) All decisions are taken by the Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister. The Prime Minister acts as the link between the President and the Council of Ministers. The Rajya Sabha is not subject to dissolution. (3) Leads Parliament and the nation, defends government policy, chairs the Planning Commission/NITI Aayog and NDC, and represents India abroad.

questions.q: Explain the emergency powers of the President of India.
questions.answer: (1) National emergency for war, external aggression or armed rebellion — only on the Cabinet's written decision; approved by Parliament within a month; the Centre can direct States and Fundamental Rights may be suspended. (2) President's Rule (Art. 356) when a State's constitutional machinery fails — the Governor rules on the President's behalf and Parliament legislates for the State; maximum three years. (3) (iii) The third type of emergency, which is called ‘financial emergency’ is declared when a situation arises whereby the financial stability or credit of India or of any part of the country is threatened. In this situation, the President can reduce the salaries of all the government officials including the judges of the Supreme Court and the High Courts. The financial emergency has not been proclaimed in India so far.

questions.q: Explain the financial powers of the President of India.
questions.answer: (1) No money bill can be introduced in the Lok Sabha without his/her prior recommendation. (2) The President gives his consent for it to be laid before the Lok Sabha before the beginning of every financial year. As regards the Annual Budget (Annual Financial Statement), it is presented in the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha may only discuss it but can not stop it from becoming law. (3) In this situation, the President can reduce the salaries of all the government officials including the judges of the Supreme Court and the High Courts. The financial emergency has not been proclaimed in India so far.

questions.q: Describe the close relationship between the legislature and the executive in India.
questions.answer: (1) The executive (PM and ministers) are members of Parliament and must become MPs within six months. (2) The Ministers hold office during the pleasure of the President, but they cannot be removed so long as they have the support of the majority in the Lok Sabha, In fact, according to the Constitution, Ministers are collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha. But only the Lok Sabha has the power to pass a no-confidence motion which if done, the Council of Minister resigns. The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha. (3) Parliament controls the executive through Question Hour, motions and approval of the budget, while the PM can advise the President to dissolve the Lok Sabha.

questions.q: Explain the functions (jurisdiction) of the Supreme Court of India.
questions.answer: (1) The Prime Minister acts as the link between the President and the Council of Ministers. The Supreme Court has three types of jurisdiction— Original, Appellate and Advisory. the one side and one or more States on the other side. (2) The Supreme Court is a court of appeal for constitutional, civil and criminal cases. It can hear appeals against the judgments of the High Courts. (3) The President may also order the suspension of the enforcement of fundamental rights. (iii) Advisory Jurisdiction: The Supreme Court has a special advisory jurisdiction in matters which may specifically be referred to it by the President of India. The Supreme Court has the powers to interpret the Constitution, and through this it has assumed the power of judicial review. It functions as the guardian of the Constitution.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Explain any six legislative powers of the President.
questions.answer: (1) (b) Legislative Powers: The President is an integral part of the Parliament and in this capacity he/she enjoys many legislative powers. (2) He/She summons and prorogues the sessions of Parliament and can dissolve the Lok Sabha on the advice of the Council of Ministers. He/She is elected by an electoral college which consists of the members of both Houses of the Parliament. (3) Dissolves the Lok Sabha- When the President dissolves the Lok Sabha, it means that the House ceases to exist till it is reconstituted after the next elections. And that is not a simple advice, but is binding. The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha. (4) The President addresses the Parliament every year at the commencement of the first session and after each general election to the Lok Sabha. (5) Without his/her assent no bill can become a law or an Act. Once the bill is passed by both the Houses, it is sent to the President for his/ her assent and with his/her assent it becomes a law or an act. If the Rajya Sabha along with its recommendations (if any) does not return it to Lok Sabha within 14 days, the bill is deemed to have been passed by both the Houses. (6) Calls a joint sitting to resolve deadlocks, issues ordinances when Parliament is not in session, and nominates 12 members to the Rajya Sabha.

or.q: Explain the meaning of the Electoral College in the Indian Presidential election. What qualifications are required for a person to be elected President of India?
or.answer: (1) He/She is elected according to the system of proportional representation by means of a single transferrable vote, and the voting is by secret ballot. He/She is indirectly elected by an Electoral College consisting of the elected members of both the Houses of the Parliament and the State Legislative Assemblies. (2) (vi) (i) a citizen of India (ii) of at least 25 years of age (iii) not hold an office (3) (ii) must have been at least a Judge of a High Court or of two or more such Courts in succession for at least five years; or (ii) (a) be a citizen of India (b) have completed the age of 35 years (c) be qualified for being elected as a Member of Lok Sabha (d) not hold any office of profit (4) (iii) be qualified for being elected as a member of the House of the People (Lok Sabha); and (5) (iv) not hold any office of profit under the government of India, any State government or under any local authority or any other authority of the said government. There is a provision for the re-election of a person who is holding or who has held the office as President. His/Her term of office is for five years, though he/she can be removed even before through impeachment.

questions.q: Explain the powers of the Supreme Court of India.
questions.answer: (1) The Prime Minister acts as the link between the President and the Council of Ministers. Members of the Lok Sabha elect the Speaker and the Deputy Speaker from among themselves. The Supreme Court has three types of jurisdiction— Original, Appellate and Advisory. the one side and one or more States on the other side. (2) The Supreme Court is a court of appeal for constitutional, civil and criminal cases. It also has the power to review its own judgment. (3) (iii) Advisory Jurisdiction: The Supreme Court has a special advisory jurisdiction in matters which may specifically be referred to it by the President of India. (4) In this situation, the President can reduce the salaries of all the government officials including the judges of the Supreme Court and the High Courts. Lok Sabha or the House of the People is the lower house. It can hear appeals against the judgments of the High Courts. (5) Guardian of the Constitution and protector of Fundamental Rights through writs (Article 32). (6) (ii) Judicial Review: The Supreme Court of India has the power to examine the validity of laws or executive orders. If on examination it is found that there has been a violation of the Constitution, the judiciary declares it to be null and void or unconstitutional. PIL has often been used on behalf of people who are poor or disadvantaged and do not have the means to approach the court. (iv) Judicial activism has concentrated on giving the disadvantaged the access to justice.

or.q: Explain the powers of the Prime Minister of India.
or.answer: (1) It is the Prime Minister who is the real head of the Union executive. The Prime Minister acts as the link between the President and the Council of Ministers. his/her powers on the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister, and their advice is binding. (2) It is on his/ her recommendations that the President appoints the members of the Council of Ministers and distributes portfolios among them. If the Lok Sabha passes a ‘no-confidence motion’, the entire Council of Ministers including PM has to resign. For the appointment of other Judges of the Supreme Court, the Chief Justice has to be consulted. (d) (i) ask questions and supplementary questions, (ii) adjournment motion and calling attention (3) All executive actions of the government of India are carried out in his/her name. He/She presides over the meetings of the Cabinet and communicates its decisions to the President. Then there is a group of ministers, called Ministers of State, some of them hold independent charges of ministries while others are attached to Cabinet Ministers. (4) The Rajya Sabha is not subject to dissolution. (5) In fact, the Prime Minister is not only the leader of the majority party, or the leader of the Parliament but he/she is also the leader of the nation. He/She is the ‘principal spokesperson’ and defender of the policies of the government in the Parliament. (6) Chairs the Planning Commission/NITI Aayog and NDC, takes decisions on defence and foreign policy and represents India abroad — the 'keystone of the cabinet arch'.

questions.q: Describe the functions of the Indian Parliament.
questions.answer: (1) Legislative: makes laws on the Union and Concurrent Lists and residuary subjects; joint sitting for deadlocks. (2) Control over the executive: Question Hour, motions and the no-confidence motion. (3) Financial: passes the budget; no tax or expenditure without its approval; money bills start in the Lok Sabha. (4) (iv) Judicial Functions: The Parliament is empowered to prescribe the number of Judges of the Supreme Court by law. His/Her term of office is for five years, though he/she can be removed even before through impeachment. (5) (b) Legislative Powers: The President is an integral part of the Parliament and in this capacity he/she enjoys many legislative powers. He/She is elected by an electoral college which consists of the members of both Houses of the Parliament. It participates in the election of the President and elects the Vice President of India. (6) Constituent: amends the Constitution and impeaches the President.
